$comment: Structural contract for the macstack/ folder. Read by project-docs (writer) and by lint (checker) — one source of truth for structure, so the two cannot drift. Anchors are byte-exact and NEVER translated; headings and prose are written in docs.language.

anchor_syntax.rule: One anchor line immediately ABOVE the heading it marks. Byte-exact: no extra spaces inside the comment. Re-inserted idempotently by docs-merge before any other write; never a reason to rewrite a document.
anchor_syntax.item_rule: An item anchor marks a FIELD INSIDE an item that a checker must locate — the cost-if-wrong clause of a ruling, the applied banner of a delta. Items themselves are NOT anchored: an item is identified by the id in its heading, which 12.3 already pattern-checks. Anchoring all 68 cases of a client-facing document would be noise for the reader and buys the linter nothing it does not already have.
anchor_syntax.generated_rule: First line of a document whose `generated` field names its source. The document is REBUILT from that source, so a hand edit is lost on the next render and 12.18 reports it as an error rather than silently overwriting. Anything a human needs to say about a generated subject goes in the document the source points BACK to — for architecture, docs/architecture.md; for a role's meaning to a person, USER-CASES.md.

case.note: X = cross-cutting, S = end-to-end scenario, Z = prohibition are RESERVED and never assigned to a role; any other uppercase ASCII letter is a role letter, chosen from the role name's first distinctive letter and recorded in roles[].cases; on collision take the next unused letter; a letter, once used, is never reassigned to a different role.

testcase.note: The case id it verifies, plus .T<n>. Traceability is built into the id: `grep 'C-06\.' ` finds every test for C-06. Numbers are never reused after a test is struck.

task.note: Milestone-scoped and permanent: M11-T9 is the ninth task of milestone 11. Chosen to match the commit convention teams already use — a subject ending '(M11-T9)' links the commit to the task for free. Never renumbered, never reused.

backlog.note: Work that is real but not yet scheduled into a milestone. On promotion the item gets a task id and the BL id is struck with a pointer to it — never silently rewritten.

milestone.note: A coherent increment someone could review or demo. Carries a done_when list of falsifiable checks.

release.note: One shipped increment, dated. A release entry is written when something reached the people who use it — not when a branch merged.

open_item.note: A = owed by the client, B = deferred engineering. Numbers are never reused after a strike-through

decision.note: Allocated in DECISIONS.md in its own commit BEFORE the rulings file is written

contradiction.note: ASCII K (U+004B) only. The Cyrillic capital KA (U+041A) renders identically and greps as absent — refuse it

readme.note: This folder's own contract, rendered for a human: the map, who owns what, the ID spaces and the loop. Generated from doc-contracts.json — the same file lint reads — so the folder cannot describe itself differently from the way it is checked.

user_cases.note: Every case heading carries an ID and a priority tag, and is followed by an acceptance list. Role sections are bound to roles[].cases in macstack.json.

test_cases.struck_form: ~~C-04.T2~~ · DROPPED in v1.9 — the acceptance bullet it covered is gone
test_cases.note: Sits between USER-CASES.md (what must be true) and reviews/ (what was found when someone checked): this document says HOW each acceptance bullet is verified. At least one test per bullet. Evidence cites a test title, never a file:line. A bullet needing human judgement is `manual` and carries steps; an `auto` test names the automated test that proves it. Regeneration is by id: update in place, never clobber hand-written steps.

renders.per_role: roles[].id → the tasks of processes[].tasks[] whose human.role matches, each with its gate (input|execute|approve) and the process it belongs to
renders.per_task: a task carrying `workflow` resolves to workflows[] → its triggers[] → the trigger's type and schedule; a task carrying `human` is started by a person on a screen and says so
renders.code: workflows[].location — where the automatic half actually lives
renders.status: workflows[].status, so a documented task that is not built cannot read as built

roles.note: WHO does WHAT and WHAT STARTS IT — the one view macstack.json holds but nobody can see without reading JSON: tasks live under processes, roles under roles[], and the trigger that moves a task is two hops away through workflows[]. Generated, because the moment it is hand-written it starts disagreeing with the spec, and a role document that disagrees is worse than none: people plan against it. The triggers section is the reverse index — schedule or event → workflows it raises → whose tasks move.

renders.stack: software[] with layers, type and agentic rating; profile.architecture_patterns
renders.entities: entities[] with their stores[] and which store holds the master
renders.workflows: workflows[] with engine, trigger, location and status
renders.integrations: connections.mcp[], interfaces[], context.plugins with what each covers

architecture.note: How this project is BUILT, for the agent that has to build in it — the human-readable face of the machine half of the spec. Generated on purpose: this is the document that rots first when written by hand, because every new collection, workflow and plugin changes it. It does NOT replace docs/architecture.md: that one holds what the spec cannot express — the measured gotcha, the argument for a decision, the trap a future reader will otherwise re-discover. Keep them apart or one of them becomes a worse copy of the other.

task_fields.tracker: REQUIRED — the id of this task in the team's own tracker. The file is the source of truth; the tracker is where the conversation happens. Both are kept current.
task_fields.spec: pointer into USER-CASES.md / BUSINESS-LOGIC.md / a design document — a reference, never a restatement
task_fields.files: paths this task is expected to touch
task_fields.acceptance: how it will be known done — named tests or TEST-CASES ids, never a line number
task_fields.blocked_by: task ids or open-item ids; an A-id here is how a client question becomes visibly load-bearing

milestone_fields.title: short
milestone_fields.done_when: a list of FALSIFIABLE checks — each one either passes or does not. 'Works well' is not a check.

tasks.note: The forward-looking half of the folder. OPEN-QUESTIONS.md §B records debt the team consciously accepted and argues why NOT to act; this document says what will be done, by when, in what order. Do not merge them: an item can be in §B for a year and only becomes a task when its trigger fires.

business_logic.note: Logic in plain words: what the product is, how it earns, what it must refuse. Never restates USER-CASES case by case.

client_table_columns: if it is wrong or missing
open_questions.note: §A is owed by the client, §B is engineering the team deferred. An §A row carries the date it was asked, because a question nobody has actually put to the client is not blocked — it is forgotten. §B argues why NOT to act now; TASKS.md says what WILL be done. Keep them apart. A §B item that becomes real work is PROMOTED, not copied: strike it with a pointer to the new task id and leave its original text untouched, so the argument for having deferred it survives next to the decision to stop deferring.

changelog.entry: ## R-YYYY-MM-DD · <milestone or version> — <what a user can now do that they could not before>
changelog.supersession: In place, never by deletion: append '**Superseded by <id>:** …' to the old entry. A changelog that edits its own past cannot be trusted about its present.
changelog.note: The curated, audience-facing half of the journal: what reached the people who use the product. log.md holds everything that happened; this holds what mattered to them. Never a git log dump — an entry claims a PROPERTY the system now has, in the words of someone who does not read code.

log.note: Append-only journal of everything that happened to this project: client material in, merges, work done, releases out. Scaffolding does not log — a freshly created folder has no entry, and that absence is intentional. CHANGELOG.md is this file's curated, client-facing derivative; the two are never merged.

handoff.note: What was handed OUT to the client and in which version. The other half of intake: without it nobody can answer 'which version did they actually review?' when their edits come back, and the edits are always against a version, never against today's file.

merge.note: A delta was ruled on and applied. The unprocessed signal: a file in inbox/ with no merge entry naming it.

work.note: What was actually built. THE DEVELOPMENT LOG. `tasks` names the task ids advanced; `what` says what now exists that did not; `notes` is the half git cannot hold — the dead end taken, the thing that turned out harder, the decision deferred. A work entry with an empty `notes` is usually a work entry not worth writing.

release.note: Something reached the people who use it. Pairs with a CHANGELOG.md entry of the same id.

inbox_manifest.note: The ONLY writable file under inbox/.

delta.note: A proposal, not an edit. Declares the bar (USER-CASES.md) and stays history. Gets one applied banner and is never otherwise revised.

rulings.note: Cost-if-wrong is written AT DECISION TIME, before the outcome is known. A retrospective cost clause is worthless.

review.note: Ships in pairs: a technical audit and its business-language twin, same date and slug, same commit. The twin rule is a WARNING until a generator exists.

prohibitions.why: Line numbers rot the moment the file above them grows. Cite a symbol name or a test title.

An ID token whose letter is a Cyrillic look-alike (U+0410 U+0412 U+0415 U+041A U+041C U+041D U+041E U+0420 U+0421 U+0422 U+0423 U+0425) greps as absent and silently breaks every cross-reference check. Compare codepoints, never glyphs.
A link resolving above the repository root does not resolve for anyone who clones only this repo.
Names of env keys only, never values — extends the existing rule 10 past resources.accesses.

inbox.do_not_copy: A source already committed in this repo at a stable path is NOT copied into inbox/ — it is cited by path. A copy diverges from its original, and inbox/ cannot be fixed afterwards.

unreadable.xlsx: Refuse: ask for a CSV export beside it and write NO log entry, so the file stays in the unprocessed set.

handoffs.note: What was sent to the client, exactly as sent. Immutable for the same reason inbox/ is: their edits come back against THIS file, and a package edited after the fact makes every returned comment unresolvable. Regenerating for a new round writes a new dated file, never overwrites.
